sections.h2: Who sets and who collects property tax in Bourbon County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Two offices in the Paris courthouse building split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) in Room 15 sets the assessment, and the Sheriff's Office in Room 104 sends the bills and takes payment.

The county directory lists the PVA at (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff at (859) 987-2130. Both keep weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The sheriff's page adds that the office closes for holidays including Good Friday, Memorial Day, Veterans Day and Thanksgiving.

sections.h2: How big is Bourbon County, and what does that mean for assessments?
sections.html:
Bourbon County covers roughly 290 square miles of mostly open, rolling farmland around Paris, with Millersburg and North Middletown as the smaller towns. Census figures put the population at 20,243 in 2025 and the housing stock at 9,399 units.

Home values here run well above neighboring Boyd County's $130,700 median. The 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner-occupied home was $229,300, and 63.7% of homes are owner-occupied. A seller with acreage can ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before assuming the figure is right.

sections.h2: When are Bourbon County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. The earlier you pay, the less you owe, and a postmark counts as the payment date under KRS 134.119.

Delinquent notices go out on February 1. At the close of business on April 15 the sheriff turns every unpaid bill over to the County Clerk, where the sheriff warns that additional significant fees apply. Anyone selling in the spring should check whether the bill has already moved.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Bourbon County tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay at the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to that address. Bills are mailed to the homeowner as postcards, so a seller whose mortgage company pays from escrow should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.

  • Accepted: cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks drawn on U.S. banks.
  • Cards are taken in person only, with a 3.5% fee. The sheriff's own example is $55.13 on a $1,575 bill.
  • Third party checks and foreign funds are refused.
  • A returned check carries a $50 fee, and a bill paid with a bad check counts as unpaid.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes. The assessment date is January 1 of each year, and the process starts with a conference with the PVA or a deputy, not with a filing.

Under KRS 133.120, you request that conference before or during the inspection period. Kentucky sets that period around the first Monday in May for two weeks, and a PVA can get approval to extend it. If you are still unhappy, you file a written petition with the County Clerk stating your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. That petition is due one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals then holds a hearing, and you bring evidence such as comparable sales, an appraisal or a repair estimate.

An appeal does not pause the bill. You pay on the value you claim, and the difference plus interest is billed if the board sets a higher figure. A taxpayer who skips the county board cannot go straight to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Bourbon County?
sections.html:
Yes, for homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled. The Department of Revenue lists the exemption at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, subtracted from the assessed value of the home.

For example, a home assessed at $200,000 is taxed on $150,900. You apply with the PVA, who is the Bourbon County office in Room 15, and the disability version must be renewed each year unless you are a service-connected disabled veteran or have been found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. The dollar amount is adjusted every two years, so ask the PVA what it is for the current assessment year.

sections.h2: What does a late Bourbon County tax bill cost in real dollars?
sections.html:
Take a bill of $2,000. Paid during November it is $1,960 after the 2% discount. In December it is $2,000. In January the 5% penalty makes it $2,100, and from February 1 through April 15 the 21% period brings it to $2,420. That is a $460 spread between paying in November and waiting until the last collection day.

The sheriff posts that last stretch as a 21% penalty period, and the 21% is the figure used above. After April 15 the County Clerk adds its own fees, and the amount you owe is whatever the clerk quotes on the day you pay. Sellers with an unpaid bill from a past year should call the clerk for that number before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: What do other Bourbon County figures show about the housing market?
sections.html:
The county issued 109 building permits in 2025, far more than Boyd County's 12, and retail sales per person in 2022 were $39,822. Median household income was $61,354 for 2020 to 2024, and 13.9% of residents were in poverty. About 94.9% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so Bourbon County is a settled place where homes change hands slowly.

That steadiness helps a seller who has the paperwork in order. A buyer's lender or title company will want the current tax bill, the deed and any lien releases on the table at closing, and each of those comes from an office within one building at 301 Main Street.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Bourbon County house?
sections.html:
Kentucky treats the tax as a personal debt of the taxpayer from the assessment date until paid, and a lien stays with the property once taxes go delinquent. Your closing agent will confirm that the bill is current.

  • Ask the sheriff whether the current year's bill has been paid, and in what period.
  • Put the buyer's mailing address in the deed's in-care-of line so the next bill reaches the right person.
  • Ask the title company how the year's tax is split between you and the buyer.
  • If a prior year is delinquent, expect a payoff figure from the County Clerk once the bill has left the sheriff.

The 2020 to 2024 median owner cost for a Bourbon County home with a mortgage was $1,424 a month, and $466 without one, so taxes sit inside a larger monthly picture for most owners.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Bourbon County property tax without a penalty?
faqs.a: December 31 pays the base amount on the sheriff's schedule, and the 2% discount applies through November 30. A 5% penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bourbon County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or by mail to that address. Card payments are accepted only in person, with a 3.5% fee.

faqs.q: What happens to a Bourbon County bill unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: The sheriff turns it over to the County Clerk for collection, and additional significant fees apply, according to the sheriff's page.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bourbon County property assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the PVA for a conference before or during the May inspection period. If that fails, file a written petition with the County Clerk by one workday after that period ends.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the Bourbon County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Homeowners aged 65 or older, or totally disabled, who apply through the PVA. The state amount is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years.
